text: We would back appointing an envoy only if the de facto authorities agree. Consultation alone would not secure our support.
The appointment would not have our delegation's support without the assent of those exercising authority in Afghanistan.
Our position is that agreement from the Afghan authorities is a prerequisite for our backing of this appointment.
Whether we support appointing the envoy depends on consent from the de facto authorities, even after consultations with other actors.
Our delegation asks that the de facto authorities be consulted. Their agreement is not a condition for our support for appointing an envoy.
Another delegation would withhold support absent consent from the de facto authorities. We record its statement and take no such position ourselves.
The appointment procedure requires consultation with the relevant Afghan actors. We describe the terms of the resolution without giving our delegation's voting conditions.
Our support for the envoy appointment does not depend on agreement from the de facto authorities. We would wait for their agreement before starting a separate local assistance project.
